#4920. Here’s what happened in crypto today

Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation.

Today in crypto, Bitcoin climbed above $80,500 as US stocks rallied following the midterm elections. Democrats won control of Congress, raising doubts about the future of the CLARITY bill, while ZachXBT identified French banking group Crédit Mutuel Arkéa as the alleged victim of a crypto theft exceeding $133 million.

Bitcoin (BTC) returned to $80,000 at Wednesday’s Wall Street open as US stocks surged following a Democratic sweep in the midterm elections.

Data from TradingView showed BTC/USD up by over 4%, having rebounded from its lowest levels in seven weeks.

Data from CoinGlass showed the price dip liquidating late BTC long positions below $76,000, while a wall of asks kept upside contained below $78,000. Total crypto long liquidations over the past 24 hours stood at $288 million.

US stock futures made swift gains on Wednesday after initially dipping overnight. S&P 500 futures fell as low as 7,490 points, their lowest level since July 31, before reaching 7,690 points, approaching new month-to-date highs.

In comments sent to Cointelegraph, James Butterfill, head of research at crypto asset manager CoinShares, saw the potential for a wider Bitcoin “relief rally” as election uncertainty faded.

Democrats have won control of both chambers of the US Congress in the midterm elections, giving the party greater influence over crypto legislation and oversight of President Donald Trump’s administration.

At the time of writing, Democrats had secured 228 House seats to Republicans’ 139, with 68 races still uncalled, according to the Associated Press. The Senate tally stood at 54 seats for Democrats and 44 for Republicans.

The result could derail the CLARITY crypto market structure bill, according to Stefan Muehlbauer, head of US government affairs at CertiK.

“The immediate read on this election result is that CLARITY bill is likely dead,” he said in comments shared with Cointelegraph, referring to both the upcoming lame-duck session and the next Congress.

Muehlbauer said he expected Sen. Elizabeth Warren and Rep. Maxine Waters, both outspoken crypto critics, to chair the Senate Banking Committee and House Financial Services Committee, respectively. Democratic control could also bring greater congressional scrutiny of Trump-linked digital asset businesses.

Onchain investigator ZachXBT has identified French banking group Crédit Mutuel Arkéa as the alleged victim of a crypto theft exceeding $133 million, warning that total losses could be higher.

On Wednesday, the pseudonymous crypto sleuth said the institution, which he described as having $235 billion in assets, was allegedly exploited over multiple days. He also suggested that additional losses may have occurred through over-the-counter (OTC) transactions that were not included in earlier estimates.

“I suspect the amount stolen is larger when accounting for OTC activity,” ZachXBT said.

The bank’s alleged involvement has not been independently verified, and ZachXBT has not disclosed how the attackers gained access to the funds.

The disclosure follows ZachXBT’s initial report on Monday, when he identified over $106 million in suspicious withdrawals from centralized exchanges.

On Tuesday, he raised the estimated losses to over $133 million after discovering another $27 million in withdrawals, some of which occurred after his initial warning.

#4918. Where to Buy Vintage Lamps (2026): 1stDibs, Etsy, and More

Listen—we’ve all fallen prey to the sort of lighting lethargy that keeps our hastily-purchased mass market table lamps on our bedside. A fluorescent task lamp might still hover over the couch, a garish flush mount shedding its harsh light. So why a vintage lamp? Because it indicates you thought about your lighting instead of going the route of a last-minute, add-to-cart impulse buy. This was deliberately searched and purchased. This was a choice made with historical design context in mind, whether it’s midcentury modern, Art Deco, or Hollywood Regency. A carefully considered piece of lighting shows your home decor chops—you’ve gone above and beyond the look of the room to consider the vibe of the room. A magnificent vintage piece communicates all that. We rounded up a few retailer options to find just the thing you need for a living room revamp, a ceiling light overhaul, or a lampshade upgrade.

We pull from 1stDibs regularly when shopping out our various home tours, where we can find the iconic works sprinkled throughout the homes of celebrities, designers, and celebrity designers. A Charlotte Perriand sconce indicates at least one substantial coffee book on the oeuvre of Le Corbusier is nearby, and a reissue of the 1960’s Gelato lamp by Italian designer Carlo Nason’s are just the tip of the iceberg. In other words: Design dorks will delight in this catalog of artifacts and iconic pieces.

Etsy is a go-to when you’re searching for a vibe rather than a specific model or designer. Try keyword searching for terms like “Art Deco” or “ginger jar lamp” and a trove of collectibles, like thrift-store-friendly finds and veritable antique gems, will surface in search. The online marketplace’s vast web of sellers means a library of vintage lighting that spans centuries and styles, often times for less than what you’d find at places like 1st Dibs and Chairish since sellers choose what they price for shipping. Contributor Lori Keong has had good luck buying pieces there from across the pond in the UK and even further afield in Slovenia, with lots of vintage sellers from the states like Philly’s Betsu and Chicago’s Spears Furnishings selling their wares on Etsy as well.

eBay brought me such things as this vintage Tarogo frog made from Ichiban rice paper that I passed up in a thrift store in Maine and thought about for months before it surfaced on the secondhand retailer. Now he sits proudly on an armoire overlooking my dining room. Which is to say: Every vintage table lamp that’s ever existed is somewhere in their backlog. Chinoiserie, vintage Noguchi lamps, kitschy conch shell lamps, Tiffany glass shades, the OG Pixar lamp—it’s all there.

Design Within Reach regularly re-issues iconic models in collaboration with the original manufacturers, giving second life to pieces like Verner Panton’s Panthella (1971), Herman Miller’s 1952 Cigar Lotus floor lamp, Greta Grossman’s 1947 Gräshoppa, and the Space Age-y Nessino table lamp which debuted in 1967, to name a few.

Rejuvenation’s vintage collection is part of a larger initiative to prevent waste. The brand’s Portland-based restoration studio team finds and restores over 3,000 antiques around the world every year to help keep them out of landfills. While the vintage pieces are one-of-a-kind finds, a large selection mirrors Rejuvenation’s midcentury modern-inspired offerings, like 20th-century brass lamps and designs with floral and gilt detailing.

Abask has some of the most beautiful antique Murano glassware lamps we’ve seen to date. Case in point: Albano Poli’s stained glass creation pictured below. The artist got his claim to fame for collaging colored glass across geometric lighting fixtures. Modern glass lamps like this one are easy to come by across Abask’s collections, as well as minimalist metal lamps and hand-painted ceramic lamps, if those better suit your style.

#4916. 5 Reasons to Fall in Love with La Quinta

Whether you’re visiting to play, explore, or simply chill, this desert paradise in California’s Coachella Valley has a little something for everyone.

Every day, from deciding whether or not to hit snooze to choosing to read a few more pages before shutting our eyes, our brains are a blur of choices—approximately 35,000 according to prevailing research. And frankly, it’s exhausting trying to make the right one every time. A vacation reboot would help… but travel planning requires even more decisions, which obviously defeats the purpose. And so the trip gets backburnered again.

What if there was a place that made choosing easy—because there’s no possible wrong answer? A land where you could decide to do all the things on the visitor’s bureau checklist, or none of them, and have an equally good time?

Enter La Quinta, California, a city of championship golf courses, towering palms, sprawling resorts with pools and spas, Old Hollywood lore, dramatic mountain backdrops, purple skies at dusk, and savory restaurants tucked into a calm corner of the Coachella Valley. It’s a place where you’re encouraged to do only what you love and what makes you feel most alive. Here in this sun-kissed slice of paradise, choose to follow the itinerary that is most Quinta-ssentially you.

There are 20 golf courses within the city limits, including the nine at the PGA West, a 2,000-acre luxury golf resort and community. Among those are the Mountain Course and the Stadium Course, which blend stunning natural beauty, manicured landscapes, challenging holes and expert designs by masters Pete Dye, Jack Nicklaus, and Greg Norman.

You can hit up the pickleball and tennis courts at Fritz Burns Park from dawn until well past dusk. The 12-acre green space also features a skate park, a children’s playground, a pool, and a dedicated area to play fetch with your pup. If you need to brush up on the rules of your chosen game, book some time with the pros at La Quinta Resort & Club, where you can rent equipment or pick up a match.

Whether you’re craving laid-back brunch bites, like the huckleberry hotcakes or double smashburgers at the farm-to-table eatery Beautiful Day, or a night on the town enjoying minty lamb chops and mai tais exploding with citrusy pucker at DSRT Club, La Quinta’s culinary scene does not disappoint.

Greet the day with Mexican delicacies like machaca or chilaquiles on the colorful porch at Casa Mendoza. If you have a hankering for south-of-the-border specialties later in the day, they also make a mean molcajete, seafood enchiladas, or tacos al pastor. Come afternoon, head to La Quinta Cliffhouse for the legendary nightly happy hour and stay for supper at sunset. There, you can put the date in date night by snacking on Medjools with bacon, blue cheese, coconut, and honey. (Pro tip: always order the gooey stone fruit however it’s served, whether as a shake, syrup or side dish—the Coachella Valley grows 95% of the dates in the U.S.) Close out the night with a slice of decadent Toll House Pie, a fixture at The Sandbar for four decades.

Those who believe it is just as important to nourish the mind as it is the body can take a walk down memory lane at the free La Quinta Museum, where the newly expanded history and culture exhibit details the people, technologies, and businesses that shaped the city, including the Cahuilla Indians, homesteaders, the railroad, and the celebrity magnet La Quinta Resort, which is celebrating its centennial this year. At the museum, visual learners can study the massive mural and a collection of photographs.

La Quinta itself is a patron of the arts. It’s hard to miss the more than 160 sculptures, murals, and decorated utility boxes installed through the Art In Public Places program. Twice a year, creatives from around the world descend on the civic center campus and turn it into a concert venue and an alfresco art gallery for a four-day festival. After admiring the artwork, head over to Old Town for locally made mementos. The charming retail district—known for its pleasing Spanish colonial architecture and vibrant sprays of bougainvillea—stocks gems at independent boutiques and galleries year-round and hosts the open-air Art on Main Street event on select Saturdays from November to April.

The area is a bonanza for outdoor activity. Bike along the base of the Santa Rosa Mountains using the paved, 2.7-mile-long Bear Creek Trail, or fix your attitude by gaining altitude on the miles of trails littered throughout the Santa Rosa and San Jacinto mountain ranges.

One popular route takes hikers a little more than six miles from the La Quinta Cove neighborhood to Lake Cahuilla, which is particularly peaceful at dawn or dusk. (The luckiest trekkers spy bighorn sheep.) Go straight to the lake to picnic, go horseback riding, or fish. Prolong your city escape by pitching a tent and camping at Cahuilla. Sunrise yoga and movie screenings are also offered lakeside.

While it’s clear there’s lots to do, know that, in the LQ, doing nothing is always on the table. Downtime happens to be a desert specialty, as there’s always a cold pool, a chaise lounge, and an umbrella drink calling your name. In fact, La Quinta Resort & Club boasts 42 pools across the 45-acre property, including a family-friendly splash zone and a more serene adults-only plunge with private cabanas and movie nights. (Don’t forget the 53 hot tubs for crisp Coachella nights.) Those who enjoy night swimming should post up at the never-closed pool at The Chateau at Lake La Quinta.

Finish the evening with stargazing and a glass of something sparkling in front of the fire pits. To really lean into relaxation, melt into a hot stone massage at Coral Spa or happily drift off while indulging in chromotherapy, a steam bath, or a dreamy scalp rub at Spa La Quinta. Or tap into an even deeper state of zen by joining a meditation or breathwork session or Sound Bath Sundays at Gather Yoga in Old Town. Plan your easiest trip ever today.

#4914. Why Women Over 50 Should Add This Underrated Carry to Their Strength Routine

“Many people think core training means crunches or planks, but one of the most functional ways to strengthen the core is by learning to resist movement,” says personal trainer Alice Jordan.

Her go-to exercise for doing exactly that? The kettlebell suitcase carry.

“Holding a kettlebell in one hand and walking with good posture forces the deep abdominal muscles, obliques, and spinal stabilizers to work continuously to keep your body upright,” explains Jordan, who specializes in strength training during perimenopause.

“For women over 50, this is particularly valuable because it develops balance, posture and stability while also improving grip strength, which is an important marker of healthy aging,” notes Jordan.

Indeed, one landmark study published in The Lancet found that lower grip strength was consistently associated with a higher risk of early death—even after accounting for age, physical activity, smoking, body size, and other cardiovascular risk factors. Notably, the researchers reported that grip strength predicted somebody’s risk of dying better than systolic blood pressure.

The single-arm kettlebell suitcase carry, adds Jordan, “also translates directly into everyday activities such as carrying shopping, lifting luggage, or playing with grandchildren, making it a highly functional exercise.”

Below, Jordan explains how to do the exercise effectively and safely.

“Aim to include the exercise 2-3 times per week as part of a strength training program. It’s particularly effective when performed after your main strength exercises or as part of your core training,” adds Jordan.

As for how heavy a weight you should use for this exercise, Jordan recommends “choosing a kettlebell that feels challenging while still allowing you to maintain perfect posture throughout the walk.”

“You should be able to resist leaning to one side, keep your shoulders level and your core engaged from start to finish,” she adds.

“As a general guide, beginners might start with around 15-20 lb, while those with more strength training experience may use 20-30 lb or heavier, depending on their ability.”

Below, Jordan highlights four key mistakes to avoid while performing this exercise.

#4913. The Men's Health 30-Day Workout Challenge

You can get moving to get in shape—but you have to commit.

SOMETIMES, THE MOST challenging part of working out is knowing what to do.

You might not have a definite goal in mind other than that you want to get moving, or that you want to look different by the time the summer season rolls around. That's okay. Not everyone is wired to constantly aspire to build muscle or run fast, following a detailed program designed to elicit peak performance and radical transformation. Just wanting to get active to live a healthier life is a worthy goal, especially if you're taking your first steps to make fitness part of your daily routine or recommitting to exercise after a break. But you have to be ready to commit to your new routine for it to be effective.

That's what the Men's Health 30-Day Workout Challenge is all about: doing something every day. Rather than limiting the focus to just one specific body part, muscle group, or type of exercise, as we have with our previous challenges, we're more interested in establishing healthy habits and introducing you to common exercise protocols that will be useful for the rest of your fitness life. Beginners can take the challenge and hold their own, while fitness pros can still push themselves to work to their full potential using these routines.

The plan is simple. You'll take on a new workout routine every day—but there will be some consistencies so you won't be constantly thrown into the deep end if you don't have a ton of experience. All of the workouts will be comprised out of a pool of just 11 exercises, which you can see demonstrated below by the program's architect, Men's Health fitness director Ebenezer Samuel, C.S.C.S.

Each week of the program will be focused on a different workout scheme, so you can get the swing of the structure and get comfortable within each protocol. The calendar will also be structured in a manner that allows you to flex all of your muscles, both figuratively and literally; Day 1 of each week will be focused on Mobility and Core, Day 2 is Upper Push/Pull, Day 3 is Lower body, Day 4 is a Mobility focus, Day 5 is Upper Push/Pull, Day 6 is an Upper/Lower/Core split, and Day 7 is all Core.

All you have to do is buy in. By Day 30 (or the bonus Day 31, if you're game), at the very least you'll have completed this challenge. If you put in max effort, you'll also be moving better, feeling fitter, and looking different than you did on Day 1.

For each interval workout, work for 40 seconds, then take 20 seconds off unless otherwise stated. Repeat for 2 rounds. The goal: Work for quality reps for each move.

You know the exercises you’re working with. Now things get fun. This week, we introduce you to AMRAPS, as many rounds as possible. You’ll work for 8 minutes in each workout this week, and your goal is to complete as many rounds of the circuit we lay out for you as possible. Don’t lose your focus on quality reps, but do aim to keep score.

This week you’ll learn the beauty of the EMOM, every minute on the minute. You’ll once again work for 8 minutes, completing the entire sequence of moves we give you every minute. Your goal: Finish all the work as quickly as possible (while still maintaining good form!) so you can rest until the start of the next minute.

You’ll once again train for 8 minutes each day, but each round, you’ll do a bit more work, by adding 1 rep to each of the exercises you must complete in every minute. #4912. 11 Best Love Seats for Small Spaces That Are Stylish (2026)

The most inviting living spaces have comfortable, functional seating options—but you don’t need a room big enough for a sprawling sectional to establish that welcoming vibe. Instead, turn to a small-space–friendly love seat, a compact sofa designed for two people, hence the name.

Even if you don’t live in a tiny apartment, a small sofa can add a romantic je ne sais quoi to a room, making a space feel more intimate, especially if you select a style with a curvy backrest that envelops guests like a hug. If you do have the space, pairing your love seat with a chaise or accent chairs can extend the footprint and add even more seating options while providing more opportunity to elevate the room’s design. One look at the vintage love seat that lives in Usher’s Atlanta home will make you a believer.

Here, find 11 designs, all between 55 and 70 inches wide, to accommodate all tastes, including the iconic mod Knoll womb settee and the more traditional leather love seat from Crate & Barrel.

Why settle for a traditional silhouette when you can have a bit of fun with your love seat? The West Elm Bogart style caught contributor Lori Keong’s eye because of its elegant bolstered back with rounded arms and a sculptural cutout base that conceals the legs. “No blocky, chubby legs or ugly hairpin appendages to stare at while I vacuum….what a concept!” she says in her review. Initially, she had some reservations about it being too stiff, classifying it as feeling similar to a medium-firm mattress. “It’s definitely firm and supportive but also not rock-hard, with just enough give—and no sag—to sleep or sit on comfortably.” Keong chose the alabaster basketweave, but if that color-upholstery combination doesn’t fit your space or style, now you can choose from 79 other options.

Serena & Lily wears the crown for coastal decor, but its offerings extend far beyond predictable patterns of sky pinstripes and gingham. With more than 125 upholstery options available—including linen, basketweave, cotton, denim, and more—in solid colors and patterns, the Spruce allows you to dress up the classic silhouette to fit a home of any style. If the slipcover is not your thing, the alternative is introducing exposed wood legs in four colorways. Regardless of your decor, the solid wood frame of this compact love seat is built to last.

For its boucle love seat, Quince uses performance fabric that is Oeko-Tex–certified, a designation that the textile in question is free of dangerous levels of harmful substances. Beneath the cozy, nubby fabric, foam cushions are supported by a hardwood frame, which is FSC-certified—a credential from the Forest Stewardship Council that specifies responsible wood sourcing. The combination of curvy, clean lines, and ivory color gives this two-seater an elevated elegance without a hefty price tag.

The Crate & Barrel Axis love seat comes in an astounding 45 leather options, including more traditional hues like caramel and bold burgundy and statement-making onyx. Silicone-based vegan materials are also available. The look, anchored by track arms and an angled back, is classic and can work just as well in an entryway as it would in a den.

The Pottery Barn Cameron power-reclining sofa may make you forget that you opted for a love seat at all. Once you hit the power button to recline and stretch out, you’ll forget all about this modular sofa’s compact stature. If your space can accommodate a few extra inches, consider adding a storage compartment between the seats for a spot to stash a mid-movie snack. Plus, the modular nature of this couch’s design means it can shift and grow with you, should you decide to place it elsewhere in your home or move to a new space altogether.

The Sabai Essential love seat looks like a hug. The low-profile seat with bench seating and plush back cushions practically begs for late-night reading sessions. Lounging is also sweeter when you know that the recycled polyester velvet is Oeko-Tex–certified as well as Global Recycled Standard 4.0-verified, a certification that affirms the content of recycled materials. And if you end up loving the seat too much, you can make use of the brand’s Repair Don’t Replace program that allows you to revive various components, like a single cushion or a scuffed sofa leg. Alternatively, if you prefer to refresh the upholstery du jour, simply swap it for a new slipcover at a fraction of the cost of a new love seat.

Joybird is the place to find a modern love seat, especially one that will go with your colorful wallpaper. The Amelia style is curvy with a twist: Its 1970s-inspired frame has a suave shape, but the cushions retain the expected rectangular configuration. Available in an eye-popping 91 colors, you should do yourself a favor and order the swatch sample box to help you choose. At 56.5 inches wide, it’s one of the smaller love seats on this list, making it ideal for teeny-tiny alcoves and nooks.

The AllModern Rae love seat comes in velvet and linen textures, giving you flexibility on whether you prefer a dressier or more casual style. Regardless of the upholstery choice, the channel stitching detail on the arms gives this compact love seat a contemporary look. The fabric is stain- and spill-resistant, but it is spot-clean–only. However, its reversible cushions let you hide a one-off oops. Also nice is that at just under 100 pounds, it’s a relatively easy sofa to move around by yourself. Toss in a few throw pillows, and you’ve got a whole new look.

Just looking at the CB2 Deseo makes us want to flop down and relax atop the two giant, pillow-like cushions filled with feathers and down. With a whopping 82 options for upholstery type and color, you can customize the love seat to fit into any room: Go for an opulent look with a rich merlot color, or tropical with the lsla Royal banana leaf linen-cotton for your sunroom.

Knoll earmarked a spot in the history of design with the Womb settee by Finnish architect Eero Saarinen, who said in 1948, “Today, more than ever, we need to relax.” Nearly 80 years later, the statement still rings true. It took Saarinen two years to make this chair, but from there, production didn't stop. Adding this piece to your furniture collection basically makes it an heirloom.

Take a page out of Brooklyn Decker and Andy Roddick’s Charlotte, North Carolina, entryway that features a small sofa with a back made of unexpected arches. The Lulu and Georgia Aimee Song Neve sofa surprises with its artfully sculpted seats that—at a medium on the firmness scale—are all about comfort. Among many upholstery and color options, it’s available in chunky boucle and garnet-and-blue stripe—a color combo that’s designer-approved.

#4907. Mercado Bitcoin says phased reopening to begin Monday, will cover losses

Customers will initially be able to view their holdings, while withdrawals and trading remain suspended pending security checks.

Brazilian crypto exchange Mercado Bitcoin said it will begin restoring customer account access Monday after a hack that blockchain analysts estimated resulted in more than $46 million in stolen assets.

In a statement to Cointelegraph, Mercado Bitcoin said customers would initially regain access through its website to view balances, statements, holdings and investments. Transfers, withdrawals and trading will resume in later phases, subject to independent security testing.

Mercado Bitcoin also pledged to use company funds to replenish assets affected by the breach, saying more than $15 million in stolen funds had already been frozen with help from the industry.

“Our trading desk is preparing to begin the necessary repurchases in domestic and international markets,” it said.

The update follows the exchange’s disclosure of a security breach on Monday, which saw attackers transferring funds from the company’s hot wallets and customer deposit addresses through standard transfers.

Addressing liquidity, Mercado said it had a strong cash position, bolstered by a $20 million investment from stablecoin issuer Tether to support operational expansion.

#4906. Jaylen Brown Is Keeping His Boston Skyrise Apartment—and Its 18th-Century Harp Too

Jaylen Brown has an 18th-century harp sitting in his living room, and that harp rules. Having a harp in your home as a newly 30-year-old man, with a professional harpist who appears when the mood strikes said 30-year-old man, is an outstanding use of free will.

“Most of the time I use my harp, it’s just me and my chef,” Brown says. A memory raced through my head: me at the end of my twenties, with a harp (broken) in my unit. And how central it would be to the social hours of 10 p.m. to 4 a.m.

Brown’s harp is not that. “It’s almost like therapy sessions,” he says.

Jaylen Brown with his cat Forky in the speakeasy of his Boston apartment design by Linda Zarifi of Zarifi Design. The project construction is by Core Group Boston, and the art advisory is by Miranda Girard. The sofa is by Charles Zana from The Invisible Collection and the ottoman is also from The Invisible Collection.

The artwork in the speakeasy is by Francisco Valverde and flanked with sconces by Apparatus. The curtain fabric is by Dedar, and the star ceiling lights are by UFO Lighting.

The wallcovering in the speakeasy is by Gregorius Pineo.

He’s a different dude in a way that makes him singular, both as a member of the National Basketball Association and as a young and famous Black man in the United States of America.

On July 1, 2026, hundreds of television talkers said “the basketball world has been turned upside down,” because Brown’s years as a Celtic were over. After nine years as half of Boston’s dynamic duo with Jayson Tatum, he was traded to Philadelphia. “It’s no beef,” Jaylen politely told reporters after a victory, beard absolutely glistening. “Might be a little lamb chops and gravy. He should stay ready at all times.” 23 days later, Brown’s new teammate became LeBron James, creating one of the strongest starting fives in NBA history. You love to see someone find a nice new gig. But as for where he rests his head, Brown held on to his place in Boston.

In the foyer, the walls are painted in Ashland Slate by Benjamin Moore. The custom table holds Brown’s championship trophy.

In the living area, the Hamilton sofa by Minotti surrounds coffee tables by Carlyle Collective. The floor lamp is by Tom Dixon and the harp is antique.

“I grew up here, age 19 to 29,” he says. “I developed here in Boston as a young man.” The feeling is mutual; October 24, his birthday, was named Jaylen Brown Day by the city. But the crib itself is doing a lot of the pulling. “There’s been other places, but this one–I created it, it was crafted by my vision,” he says. “This one felt the most like home.”

He hired a team to bring his dreams to life. Linda Zarifi, of Zarifi Design, was his interior designer and collaborator. “The first thing he said was ‘I don’t want a dining table,’” Zarifi says. “And I’m like, ‘Where are you going to…eat?’”

The answer was a 22-foot banquette, built for most home activities. “I wanted to open the space up. I wanted gold. I wanted a see-through wine cellar. She went and found it all,” Brown says.

The custom dining banquette is upholstered in Crescendo Suede by Kravet and the glass and metal tables are also custom by Jamie Cumming. The TG-10 Sling dining chairs are by Gratz Industries and the wall sconces are by Gubi. Inside the frame on the wall is a proclamation from the city of Boston for Jaylen Brown Day.

Brown in the dining 22-foot banquette playing chess.

The result is a 4,000 square-foot apartment overlooking Boston’s Financial District. Brown purchased the downtown space at the end of 2023 and reworked it over the last two years. Outside, the apartment is a brief 15 minute walk from the TD Garden, home to Brown’s former team, the Boston Celtics. Inside, Italian marble bathroom floors, 24-karat fixtures that Brown calls “jewelry for the bathroom,” a custom suede pool table, a party-ready speakeasy, and that see-through wine cellar.

There’s also the medical hyperbaric chamber one step from his bed, one of the truest signs that he is a single man.

Jaylen is figuring it out in real time, and he’s letting us watch and listen.

The trophy case in the speakeasy is a custom design by Zarifi and fabricated by Jamie Cumming of Loki Custom Furniture.

A shelf in the speakeasy holds a collection of Brown’s memorabilia.

A chandelier by John Pomp hangs over the bar area with stools by Blackman Cruz upholstered in a leather by Holly Hunt.

Kashmir barstools from Resident tuck under the kitchen counter. The flushmounts are from RH and the kitchen cabinets are painted in Cheating Heart by Benjamin Moore.

They say he’s not new to this. In 2020, five days after George Floyd was murdered, he drove 15 hours from Boston to our hometown of Atlanta to lead a march. The same guy who took the swooshes off his Nikes and now has his own shoe company (with custom closets by Molteni&C to house his own collection). And the same guy who uses this home to stream with Lil Baby and to display art and artifacts dedicated to his family.

“The things that he would splurge on are the things that mattered most to him,” Zarifi says. There’s the commissioned portrait in cracked glass by Simon Berger of his grandmother in the foyer. “For him, his flex was his harp.”

Brown seated on a bench in the primary bedroom. The custom bed is upholstered in a fabric by Mokum Textiles. The pendants by Apparatus hang over custom nightstands flanking the bed.

“I had them recreate the bedding and the comforter of the Four Seasons,” Brown says. The bedding is custom from Crem & Co. Brown’s hyperbaric chamber is beside the bed.

“I love the tempered glass,” Brown says. The closet design is the Glis Closet System by Molteni&C. The pendant light is by Henge.

The custom vanity in the primary bathroom is flanked with sconces by Articolo. The fittings are by Dornbracht.

The tub and counters are topped in a Pietra Grey stone and the ceiling is painted Ashland Slate by Benjamin Moore.

The Sally armchair in the primary bedroom is by Minotti and covered in Holly Hunt fabric.

He hasn’t taken lessons yet, good for no more than an impassioned glissando. What he does do, however, is soak in the sounds from Li Shan Tan, the principal harp for the New Haven Symphony Orchestra, who plucks from his palace. “From time to time, when she is not around, I go and I try to recreate some sounds.”

#4902. This Picture-Perfect Suburban Kitchen Is an Argument for Maxed-Out Storage, Smart Appliances, and Custom Furniture

The house had everything a young family could want: classic Georgian architecture, a picturesque setting in East Glenview, Illinois, and a neighborhood where kids ride bikes and golden retrievers lounge in the sunshine. For a Chicago couple with three young sons, it checked nearly every box. The kitchen, however, was another story. Its awkward layout, dated appliances, and surprisingly scant storage made it feel ill-equipped for the demands of a family of five.

Fortunately, the problem was one that could be solved. Elizabeth Smolcich, principal interior designer of Glenview-based firm Mason & Brass, saw its potential. “We knew we’d have to do a heavy lift to make the kitchen feel like ours,” says homeowner Marie Gould. “Elizabeth had a vision for it that made it much more functional and kid-friendly for our family.”

Kitchen layout, before and after. A wider doorway improves the flow between kitchen and living room, while removal of a corner booth created space for a larger island and the potential for more seating.

Homeowner Marie Gould with her sons in the renovated kitchen

Smolcich started by widening the opening between the kitchen and living room just enough to let Gould easily eyeball what her boys, ages seven, six, and three, are up to while she’s cooking. And removing an awkwardly positioned corner booth, one that was too small to seat four comfortably but obtrusive enough to impede the 450-square-foot room’s flow, gave the designer enough space to expand and center a new kitchen island.

This island, topped with smoky quartzite, provides plenty of counter space for prepping meals or rolling out dough, and even has enough room for the boys to perch on when they want a close-up view of the action. Above the island, Smolcich installed schoolhouse-style fluted glass pendants, which the couple loved for their timeless appeal. The most significant addition came in the form of a custom banquette that looks built into the island but is actually a movable bench. The family slides this upholstered piece to one side of their dining table, which can expand from 66 inches to 96 inches, when they’re hosting a crowd. (They’re expecting more than 40 friends and family for Thanksgiving this year.)

This is a family that loves to entertain, says the designer. A double oven, then, was a necessity, as was a serious range that allows Gould to sear a steak with restaurant-quality char. Gould discovered the ultimate time-saving mom hack with her smart SKS range, which features a rapid preheat function and can boil a pot of water for pasta in just 60 seconds. It has both an induction cooktop to prevent tiny hands from burns as well as four gas burners that satisfy even the pickiest of eaters.

Two ovens were a necessity for the homeowners’ busy household. Brizo Rook faucets and Visual Comfort Parkington sconces, both in brass, warm up the space.

The designer flanked the stove with open shelving to keep oils and seasonings within easy reach. The dual gas and induction SKS range features Smart Knob technology.

“They’re big on texture,” says Gould of her family. “They love a sear and a proper crust, which is no problem with this.” (That said, she says she personally appreciates the range’s sous vide capability best, although the SKS Smart Knobs, with LED screens for each knob to monitor heat levels and time remaining, are a close second.)

Over the range Smolcich installed hidden, integrated built-in storage to hold Gould’s go-to oils and seasonings. “We took advantage of any and all real estate,” explains the designer. “We can make anything beautiful. That’s not the hard part of what we do. The hard part is making it wildly functional. If you feel like you have to go out of your way to retrieve something, you’re never going to love it.”

Designer Elizabeth Smolcich’s mood board of furniture, lighting, and surfaces

Hence the dual SKS dishwashers staggered from the Kohler prep sink in the island to the main Kohler sink (with a custom cutting board) on the perimeter; the pantry wall (painted Benjamin Moore Black Iron); an appliance garage (housing Gould’s toaster, blenders, mixer, and coffee maker); and a beverage bar with a 24-inch second fridge stocked with her kids’ juice boxes.

Prominently displayed is a treasured side-by-side picture frame with a photo of Gould’s parents baking with her oldest son next to a handwritten copy of their family’s banana bread recipe.

“That’s what this kitchen is to them,” says Smolcich. “In a few years, those boys will be sitting at that banquette doing their homework. We took this big house with a kitchen built for just a few people and made it one for a family.”

The beverage bar includes an under-the-counter refrigerator where the kids can grab their juice boxes.

#4901. A Reader’s Guide to the Many Sexy Roles of Alexander Skarsgård

Hollywood initially tried to make the 50-year-old star into a traditional hunk. He got weirder—and hotter—instead.

FAR TOO OFTEN, today’s Hollywood hunks deny their beauty to play a cavalcade of schmucks, freaks, and losers with funny accents, hiding in prosthetics because they think this will transform them into “serious” actors in the public eye. But this strategy doesn’t always pay off. Leo spent two hours and 42 minutes running around in a plaid bathrobe and messy man bun only to lose the Best Actor Oscar to Michael B. Jordan, who played a smokeshow vampire with a spit kink (and his identically sexy twin).

It’s best not to underestimate someone with undeniable sex appeal and unquenchable blood lust, as Alexander Skarsgård knows all too well from his years playing Eric Northman on True Blood. The role not only made Stockholm’s native son a household name in America, but an instantly recognizable sex symbol. Not that he needed much help from Hollywood. Skarsgård is 6'4" of muscle with anime bone structure. He’s 50, but doesn’t age in human years. He makes us mere mortal men all look, and feel, lesser than. The scion of Swedish acting royalty comes from a place where everyone kind of looks like that, yet he’s been named Sweden’s Sexiest Man Alive five times.

“After my first job, I was on a stupid ‘sexy hunky hot list’ and then people didn’t take me seriously,” Skarsgård told the The Sunday Times in 2022. “If you want characters with depth but have been labelled ‘a dude who takes his shirt off’, you’re not going to get those offers.” At the time, he was promoting The Northman, for which he’d packed on 25 additional pounds of muscle to play a Viking warrior prince, and spent most of his screen time shirtless, delivering the exact sort of performance that theoretically typecast him in the first place.

From scanning his filmography, it’s clear that at a certain point, Skarsgård decided to lean into his lot in life as an unapologetic sex symbol. Over the past two decades, he’s slowly gravitated toward roles that don’t attempt to soften or normalize his hunkiness, portraying a diverse range of characters who all just happen to be ridiculously hot in films and television shows that play with his beauty, what it means, and how it messes with the rest of us.

In his latest, Wicker, Skarsgård plays a literal object of desire, the purest distillation of his on-screen persona as a sweet and (still, somehow) sexy magical dildo who loves doing chores and adores his fishmonger wife (Olivia Colman), causing hysteria in a village full of dumbasses who have no idea how to treat or fuck a woman. In other words, he’s Alexander Skarsgård.

Ben Stiller’s comedy classic is built around the premise that Jerry Stiller’s son and Owen Wilson and Benedict Cumberbatch are male models. A fun piece of trivia is Skarsgård was inserted as one of Derek’s United Nations of conventionally attractive roommates. Baby faced Meekus is hilariously bad at bitchy teenage girl humor and loves orange mocha frappuccinos. He gets in a gasoline fight in the first installment that results in a fiery death, but returns for the sequel in a brief cameo, perfectly cast as the original man.

Skarsgård became a star when this show was a very good gothic soap opera people held in the same regard as many of the HBO classics that were on at the time, but it has faded from memory due to completely spinning off its axis in later seasons. But his role as Eric Northman, a sexy, menacing Viking prince who carries himself with regal arrogance when he first washes up in Louisiana, remains an indelible performance. He’s a kind of Magneto/Lestat figure, who believes in vampire superiority and humans primarily as food, then slowly reforms.

This remake of the 1971 Sam Peckinpah classic is a bad, hamfisted W. Bush era culture war movie (released three years late), in which James Marsden, as a pretentious, Harvard-educated lib Hollywood screenwriter, is pitted against Skarsgård, who plays a God-, guns-, country music and football-loving redneck. But the use of Skarsgård is symbolically correct: As a rugged man’s man who works with his hands, hulks over Marsden’s effete snob, and represents all Marsden’s shortcomings and insecurities.

The Charismatic Cult Leader: The East (2013) & The Stand (2020)

Two roles that trade on Skarsgård’s magnetism, casting him as cult leaders. One is Benji, an eco-terrorist ringleader in The East, which was overshadowed by Kelly Reichardt’s superior eco-terrorist anti-thriller Night Moves from the same year, but is also very good. Skarsgård begins the film as a hirsute, politically radical Jim Morrison. The role generally strips a lot of his raw tools away but he proves he still has the juice, running his operations with the certitude of a self-righteous zealot, taking full advantage of his implicit understanding that everyone will do what he says because they all want to fuck him.

That same energy is twisted evil in the less-than-stellar and largely forgotten Paramount+-produced adaptation of Stephen King’s The Stand from 2020. Skarsgård is having a blast here, clearly tapped in and comfortable with the cheap, fatty, made for TV vibes. He plays Randall Flagg, an infamous demonic anti-Christ figure in King lore, who also swaggers around making dark, grand pronouncements because he knows everyone is dreaming about him…and wants to fuck him.

The Mythological Figure: The Legend of Tarzan (2016) & The Northman (2022)

These are the two loin cloth roles that make best use of Skarsgård as physical clay. The first was a bid for a franchise at a more conventional phase of Skarsgard’s career. It’s a horribly problematic text about a Lawrence of Arabia raised by gorillas in the Congo, released at what was probably the latest moment in modern history anyone could’ve possibly thought this IP could still work in any context. And yet, Christoph Waltz is the bad guy, Margot Robbie is Jane, Samuel L. Jackson turns in a peak performance. It doesn’t really matter, because the movie doesn’t work. The one very funny, deeply horny beat, however, is Tarzan and Jane’s meet cute, when Robbie happens upon a still uncivilized, dirt and grime covered Skarsgård in the jungle, who emerges from the brush, towers over her, then sniffs her from head to toe, which is a shameless, incredibly erotic romantasy/soft porn scenario.

The Northman on the other hand, rules, and might just be the best movie in director Robert Eggers’s burgeoning and impressive filmography. I still wonder to this day how it wasn’t a bigger deal (likely the mid 2022 Covid-era release date, but still). Skarsgård leaves it all on screen in this folklore epic, near naked in the snow, in the mud, in the waves, shredded and extremely believable as a raider scaling ramparts with a battle axe, lurching through villages as they’re pillaged and burned.

The Alpha Scumbag: Big Little Lies (2017-2019)

“Biggest scumbag Alexander Skarsgård has ever played” is quite a distinction, but it has to be Perry Wright, a manipulative, abusive, domineering, womanizing monster who entwines magnetic, toxic sex with serial spousal abuse in David E. Kelly’s Shakespearean, rich, white wine-momsploitation thriller. He plays one of the few believable on-screen partners Nicole Kidman has ever had, arm candy who wears the fuck out of tailored suits. He’s a striking contrast to the show’s other husbands, all older boring, brunette, beta boys. He’s a perfect-from-a-distance husband and father, the on-paper exemplar of a certain anachronistic masculinity, and also the epitome of damaged male evil. Which is why Perry’s Orient Express style group murder is the climax of the first season of the show.

The Tech Demigod (The Odin of Codin): Succession (2018-2023)

A highly unlikely proposition. Harry Melling (who most probably still know best from his role as Dudley Dursley in the Harry Potter films) is Colin, a nebbishy mama’s boy with an aptitude for devotion in a barbershop quartet. Colin’s meetcute is delivering a back alley blowjob with little preamble to Skarsgård’s Ray, the hung final boss of leather daddies in the sweetest BDSM rom-com since Secretary. As Ray, Skarsgård communicates almost entirely via squinting, grunting, monosyllabic responses, and direct commands, yet is a completely alluring masculine ideal. His hobbies are waxing his motorcycle, watching shit on his phone while he eats, wrestling in assless unitards as foreplay, and reading Knausgaard. You can smell the sandalwood, cedar and tobacco wafting off the screen.

In which Skarsgård finally, inevitably plays a robot. This is a darkly comedic, but also occasionally saccharine, Apple TV+ series about a Wall-E war machine. His character, known only as Murderbot, has found a way to disable the guardrails that would otherwise force him to obey protocols programmed by the nefarious Weyland-Yutani style corporation who created him, and uses this freedom to consume our garbage TV shows. Murderbot expresses a professed disinterest in humanity, and hates eye contact; It’s a weird, flat, funny performance that ultimately lands halfway between Pedro Pascal in The Mandalorian and Peter Weller in Robocop. Skarsgård is a completely believable robot in a show that also serves as a metaphor for autism.

Flatbush local, former mayor of New York City

#4898. An Easy 3 Miles with On’s Cloudsurfer 3

After years of stubborn loyalty to another brand, could one city jog make a longtime runner reconsider his shoes?

After just a mile in On's Cloudsurfer 3, it dawned on me—I’ve been far too hard-headed when it comes to my choice of running shoes.

For years, I held steadfastly to a particular brand and style, year after year, run after run. When one pair wore out, leaving my shins aching and feet tender, I’d quickly order a replacement online without even a thought of pivoting. Different colors and patterns kept it interesting, but that was the extent of my athletic audacity.

Truthfully, it wasn’t about brand loyalty. I wouldn’t dare try another shoe by the same company. It was more a case of preferring what I had grown used to in the past decade over the potential thrill of experimentation.

When I was asked to take On’s Cloudsurfer 3 for a jaunt, I was skeptical. Not that the shoes couldn’t or wouldn’t be great—it’s On, after all, a company renowned for exceptional technology and an ultralightweight feel to their sneaks—but that they’d be able to win over someone like me.

Still, I was game. The assignment called for my honest opinion during a three-mile run, and I was ready to break out of my rut (or at least try to). So I laced up and headed out on a beautiful early-fall Sunday afternoon in New York City. Here’s how it went.

I was intrigued even before I took my first step. Putting on Cloudsurfer 3, it immediately felt lighter than my go-to shoes. That surprised me, considering the minimal weight of my faves is what originally attracted me to them. The knit-mesh on the outside of the Cloudsurfer 3 was light and airy, and the inside was plush in all the right places (including the generous ankle collar) without being overbearing.

Yet, I knew the bigger test was to come. As a long-time sand volleyball player, I’ve developed a harder-than-necessary plant of my foot when I run, so I tend to need soft cushioning from a shoe.

Heading outside, I took a breath and set off down the sidewalk. The first strides were cautious, as I focused on the new sensation. The initial feedback was encouraging. It all felt effortless and soft, which I later would learn was due to On’s proprietary Surreal™ Superfoam with CloudTec®. I knew of On’s “run on clouds” tagline, but now I was feeling it in action, and I liked the smooth, soft ride I was experiencing.

I was a half-mile in when I hit my first red light—an unavoidable hazard of city running—giving me a moment to stop and reflect. “That was easier than usual,” I thought. I appreciated the secure feel of my ankle without it being too constricting, and my foot didn’t shift at all in the propulsive phase of my gait. The toe box was nice and comfy.

Pleasantly surprised so far, I changed my route on the fly and headed into Central Park. I wanted to test out the Cloudsurfer 3 on the oval around the Great Lawn . . . and enjoy an uninterrupted 0.55-mile loop.

I was breathing a little heavier at this point, but I noticed something about the shoe: It gave me the sensation of running downhill, even on a flat surface. I also felt what I’d call a “rebound” effect as each foot touched down and lifted off. This energy return made me feel faster than usual, with a burst of extra power on my “swing” phase and increased confidence in my mechanics. Could the Cloudsurfer 3’s mere 10.8 ounces per shoe be the difference maker?

I don’t know if it was the refreshing chill in the air, the clearer path than I’m used to in the city, or an extra “oomph” that the shoes’ softness provided, but I did a doubletake when seeing my 10:02 split time at the end of the second mile—well ahead of my typically slow 11-minute pace.

After two treks around the Great Lawn, I was back on the paved trail that leads out of the park. The sweat was beading despite a comfortable temperature in the high 60s, but I was enjoying the workout.

By the last mile, my legs were feeling good thanks to the easy two miles prior. I was in “go” mode and barely noticed my shoes. I decided to switch up my routine and finish with a series of sprints on the city blocks—fast bursts between intersections, with short rests at red lights.

Everything was still flowing smoothly: an effortless “lift” on each step, a seamless heel-to-toe transition, and no reverberations from the hard sidewalk and street underfoot. The last third of the run seemed to fly by, and I was more than happy with yet another sub-11-minute mile. I also realized that a fresh scrape on my ankle from a volleyball match earlier in the week, which I had been worried about aggravating during the run, was completely pain free; there was no chafing whatsoever.

When I took this assignment, I knew I’d likely be impressed with On’s Cloudsurfer 3. This is no ordinary sneaker, after all, but one designed with Swiss precision and an array of features celebrated by regular Joes and top-tier marathoners alike.

What I wasn’t quite ready for was the thought that maybe, just maybe, it was time to move on from my old standbys. I do know one thing as I reflect on the experience: My daily runs will be in On’s Cloudsurfer 3 because its soft, smooth ride made this run feel effortless.
